name: Gallium

to.site: US defense and chip electronics hub, Northern Virginia

what_it_is: A soft metal used to make fast chips and radar parts.
used_for: Radar, 5G and power chips, LEDs, compound semiconductors.
status_detail: China banned gallium/germanium/antimony exports to the US in Dec 2024; the ban on US-bound shipments is suspended until 2026-11-27 after the Oct 2025 Trump-Xi meeting, but the metals stay on the licence list and military end users remain barred. Not confirmed whether it will be extended past Nov 27 2026.
evidence: USGS profile puts China at about 99% of primary gallium output in 2024.

name: Germanium

to.site: US optics and chip makers, Dallas

what_it_is: A metal used in infrared optics and fibre and in some chips.
used_for: Night vision, fibre optics, solar cells for satellites, chip parts.
status_detail: China banned gallium/germanium/antimony exports to the US in Dec 2024; the ban on US-bound shipments is suspended until 2026-11-27 after the Oct 2025 Trump-Xi meeting, but the metals stay on the licence list and military end users remain barred. Not confirmed whether it will be extended past Nov 27 2026.
evidence: Estimates of China's share range from about 59% to 70% depending on source; USGS profile did not list it above 50%.
contested_note: Share figures differ by source and definition.

name: Antimony

from.site: Xikuangshan antimony mine area, Lengshuijiang, Hunan

what_it_is: A metal used in flame retardants, batteries and ammunition.
used_for: Defense, flame-retardant electronics, some chip processing.
status_detail: China banned gallium/germanium/antimony exports to the US in Dec 2024; the ban on US-bound shipments is suspended until 2026-11-27 after the Oct 2025 Trump-Xi meeting, but the metals stay on the licence list and military end users remain barred. Not confirmed whether it will be extended past Nov 27 2026.
evidence: China produces roughly half of world antimony by secondary estimates.
contested_note: Estimates of China's share vary (about 48% to 50%+).

name: Heavy rare earths (dysprosium, terbium)

to.site: Northern Virginia data center cluster, Ashburn

what_it_is: Special metals that make magnets keep working at high heat.
used_for: Magnets for cooling fans, hard drives, motors, defense systems.
status_detail: April 2025 licence rules on seven heavy rare earths remain in force. The broader Oct 2025 expansion (MOFCOM Announcement 70) is suspended to 2026-11-10; reports say the truce is extended to 2027-01-10 but no new MOFCOM notice was found as of mid-Oct 2026.
evidence: IEA: China has over 90% of rare earth refining.

name: Rare earth permanent magnets

to.site: US auto and defense electronics hub, Detroit

what_it_is: Very strong small magnets used in motors and drives.
used_for: Server fans, hard drive motors, EVs, missiles, robotics.
status_detail: Licences needed for magnets containing dysprosium or terbium since April 2025; that part was never suspended. Oct 2025 rules are paused until at least 2026-11-10 (maybe 2027-01-10).
evidence: IEA: nearly 95% of permanent magnet production is in China.

name: Battery-grade graphite

to.site: US battery and data center backup supply chain, Ohio

what_it_is: The carbon material that forms the negative side of lithium-ion batteries.
used_for: Batteries for data center backup power and EVs.
status_detail: Dec 2023 licence rules apply. Tighter end-use checks on US-bound graphite were suspended until 2026-11-27 and not confirmed extended.
evidence: IEA: over 90% of processed graphite comes from China.

name: Lithium-ion battery cells and cathode tech

from.site: CATL HQ and cell plants, Ningde, Fujian

to.site: Northern Virginia data center cluster, Ashburn

evidence: Share of cell production not verified.

name: Mature-node (older) chips

to.site: US auto and industrial electronics hub, Detroit

what_it_is: Older, cheaper chips (28nm and larger) used in power supplies, cars and servers.
used_for: Power management, microcontrollers, auto, defense electronics.
status_detail: China is adding mature-node capacity fast. The 2025 Nexperia split showed Western users could be cut off from Chinese-packaged chips.
evidence: TrendForce (2024): Chinese makers to hold about 25% of mature-node capacity of top 10 foundries.

what_it_is: Basic chips (diodes, transistors) finished in China for a Dutch-owned firm.
status_detail: After the Dutch government seized control of Nexperia in Oct 2025 China restricted its chip exports, then the China unit moved to local wafer supply. Present status not verified.
evidence: Nexperia China is a split-off unit sourcing wafers from Chinese suppliers (secondary report).

name: Myanmar heavy rare earth ore
what_it_is: Ore from Myanmar rebel-held mines that Chinese plants turn into magnet metals.
used_for: Feedstock for heavy rare earths in magnets.
status_detail: Flows are disrupted by fighting in Kachin. Reuters reports China threatened to halt purchases from KIA areas.
evidence: About 12,944 t of rare earth oxides and metals went from Myanmar to China in Jan-May 2025.

name: DRC cobalt and copper (Chinese-owned)
what_it_is: Congo mines owned by Chinese firms, with ore refined in China.
used_for: Cobalt and copper for batteries and data center power cabling.
status_detail: CMOC owns 80% of Tenke Fungurume and 71.25% of Kisanfu. China's refining share not verified.
evidence: DRC is about 60% of world cobalt (IMF, via press); Chinese firms reportedly control over 70% of DRC copper output.
